subject: Mid-run token growth incident — coordinated mitigation plan & customer note
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] mid-run token growth observed — initial telemetry and trace attached

Heads up — automated telemetry detected an unexpected jump in per-request token generation for several Fluxon Labs tenant requests starting ~08:55 PDT. P50 stayed flat but P95/P99 climbed ~2.1x for a ~20m window. Initial hypothesis: transient KV-cache churn causing de-optimized kernel scheduling and longer decode loops.

What I attached: runtime-trace-20270915.zip (flattened traces + sample request ids)

Immediate impact: increased tail latency for streaming gen endpoints (not embeddings). Throughput didn't drop across the pool, but effective per-request token cost spiked which triggered some request pacing on client side.

Acute mitigations I can do now (need org approvals for customer-facing actions):
- Reprime relevant prefix cache keys for Fluxon tenant (low risk, ~2m ops)
- Apply a short per-tenant soft-QPS cap (10m window) to limit ephemeral token-growth amplification
- Temporarily tighten batch-window to favor latency over throughput for the affected model (will reduce efficiency ~5–8%)

Questions for product/CS: do we want to notify Fluxon now with a short notice, or hold until we've run the prime + observe? If we notify: who owns customer comms?

—Karthik

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-15T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] mid-run token growth observed — initial telemetry and trace attached

Thanks Karthik — clear summary. A few asks from product and ops coordination perspective before we act: 

1) Roadmap/longer-term: is this a quirk of the current kernel selection for the model family (i.e., will a planned quantization/kernel change on the roadmap address this), or is it purely cache warmness and workload-shaped? I want a 1–2 sentence answer we can pass to leadership.

2) Customer comms: David, please draft a short proactive note we can send if the mitigation takes >30m or if we apply a soft cap. Keep it apologetic + action-focused. Avoid technical jargon for the first note.

3) Decision matrix: I authorize the prefix re-prime immediately. For soft-QPS cap or batch-window tightening, pause until we see the post-prime telemetry unless latency remains >1.8x baseline at P95. Marcus — can you confirm rollback steps for batch-window changes and expected perf delta?

Also flagging product priority: if this repeats, I'd like a short roadmap ticket to evaluate kernel-selection heuristics by decoupling KV eviction behavior from scheduling decisions. 

On customer notification: I'd prefer to avoid alarming language; propose a short note saying we observed degraded tail latency for a subset of requests, we've applied mitigations, and we're monitoring. David will take first stab.

—Marissa

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-15T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] mid-run token growth observed — initial telemetry and trace attached

Replying inline to your asks: 

> 1) Roadmap/longer-term: is this a quirk of kernel selection or purely cache warmness?
Short: both. The model's attention/decoder pattern interacts poorly with our current kernel fallback when KV cache entries expire rapidly; that makes certain tokens loop into the slower path more often. Ongoing work (Q4 kernel tuning + per-arch heuristics) should reduce frequency — but it won't eliminate cases where customer-side request patterns cause abrupt cache churn. I recommend a radar ticket to evaluate heuristic thresholds and an engineering spike to test synthetic churn patterns.

> Marcus — confirm rollback steps for batch-window changes and perf delta
Marcus: If we shorten batch-window, rollback is a single config change (feature flag) — rollback takes effect within 30s and we can revert safely. Expected perf delta: ~5–8% higher cost per token, ~10–20ms lower P95 latency in the observed footprint.

Actions taken now: 
- Prefix re-prime started at 10:05 PDT (targeted keys for Fluxon tenant).
- Observability: enabled high-frequency sampling to track p50/p95/p99 every 15s for the next 30m.

If we still see >1.8x P95 after 10:40, propose we apply a 10m soft-QPS cap and concurrently shorten batch-window. I'll execute on approvals flagged below.

Approvals requested: 
- Product (Marissa) to allow soft-QPS cap and batch-window tighten if metrics remain degraded after prime.
- CS (David) to approve the customer-facing message if we plan to notify.

—Karthik

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-15T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: DRAFT: Short note to Fluxon Labs — observed tail latency spike

Marissa / Karthik — draft below for quick review. If you sign off, I'll send to Samantha Reed + ops@fluxonlabs.com.

Subject: Brief status — degraded tail latency for a subset of requests (we’re on it)

Hi Samantha / Fluxon Ops team,

We want to make you aware that earlier today we observed a temporary increase in tail latency for a subset of request patterns to your GenAPI endpoints. Our engineering team has applied targeted mitigations and is actively monitoring the environment. At this time the issue is contained to a small percentage of requests and we do not expect customer data to have been affected.

If you notice any customer-facing impact on your end, please forward examples (request id + timestamp) to ops@redwood.com and we’ll prioritize those. We’ll follow up with a brief summary once we’re confident the stability has returned to baseline.

Apologies for the disruption — we aim to keep Fluxon running smoothly and appreciate your patience.

Best,
David Kim
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Please suggest edits — keep it short and avoid deep technical details. If we plan to apply a soft cap, call that out as a temporary step we may take to reduce customer-side noise.

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-16T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Post-mortem next steps + customer note approved (send when metrics stable)

Thanks all for the quick coord. Final decisions and next steps: 

1) Actions taken (completed):
- 2027-09-15 10:05 PDT: Prefix re-prime executed (targeted keys for Fluxon).
- 2027-09-15 10:10–10:40 PDT: High-frequency sampling enabled; P95 returned to ~1.05x baseline by 10:30.
- No immediate throughput drops observed; cost per token returned to baseline over the hour.

2) Approvals and contingency: 
- Product (me) approved a short 10m soft-QPS cap only if P95 remained >1.8x after the prime. We did not need to apply the cap.
- Marcus confirmed batch-window change can be rolled in/out quickly; we did not change batch-window during this incident.

3) Customer messaging:
- David: approved to send the draft from 12:30 on 9/15 once metrics are stable — please add one-line that we did not need to apply service caps.
- Send timing: first follow-up should be sent once P95 is stable for 60m.

4) Engineering follow-ups (roadmap asks):
- Create a short spike (INF-4821) to characterize kernel-selection failures under aggressive KV churn; deliverable: reproduce in synthetic harness + propose two heuristic knobs by EoQ4.
- Add a small telemetry flag to detect token-growth patterns preemptively and auto-trigger a prefix re-prime for tenants (opt-in / feature flag).

5) Artifacts: attached runbook + trace for retention.

Attachments: p50-p95-runbook.md, runtime-trace-20270915.zip

I'll file a concise incident note in Confluence tonight summarizing the timeline. Thanks to Karthik and Marcus for the fast triage and to David for the customer-ready note.

—Marissa
